globalDemand.value: Global rubber-black demand ~13.6 mn t growing ~4% a year; specialty blacks ~1.1 mn t growing 4-5% (2025-30); company mid-term outlook: global carbon black demand ~3% CAGR

indiaTrade.value: India's carbon black exports +12% in FY26 to 4.44 lakh t; imports −11% to 1.30 lakh t; net exporter since FY22. Western markets have added little capacity; EU sanctions on Russian carbon black; China's anti-involution policy

imports2026.value: Russian carbon black imports into India fell ~40% YoY in Jan-Jun 2026 (6,626 t → 3,989 t) as Ukrainian strikes hit Russian refineries; Chinese imports rose ~52% (20,650 t → 31,433 t) at ~$1.3/kg vs ~$1.0/kg for Russian material; total imports ~70 kt in H1 CY26, broadly stable

europe.value: Western Europe imports ~500 kt of carbon black a year, ~80% from Russia before sanctions; India supplies ~100 kt. No EU duty on carbon black; the India-EU FTA removes the 4.5% duty on Indian tyres (Europe ~one-third of India's tyre exports)

tyres.value: Indian tyre industry grew 7-8% in FY26; industry expects high single-digit growth over FY27-29; tyre exports +9% in FY26; leading tyre makers near 90% utilisation with fresh capex for FY27. ~55% of tyre sales go to replacement

usTariffs.value: In Oct-2025 the US tariff cost PCBL ~₹70 cr a year of EBITDA (effective ~20% on ~₹350 cr of US carbon black sales); after the Feb-2026 India-US deal, Indian carbon black carries a lower US tariff than Asian and Middle East rivals, and China and Russia face higher barriers

feedstock.value: CBFS (crude-linked) is ~90-95% of material cost; ~90% imported, ~75% from the US Gulf Coast. Coal-tar-based oil (CBO), used by Chinese makers, costs ~$150-200/t more; PCBL plans coal-tar distillation to diversify

domesticOvercapacity.value: Management listed 'significant capacity addition in India' and 'surplus domestic capacity' among FY26 headwinds; India imports 8,000-10,000 t a month at low prices, pressuring spot prices

timeline.what: Russian carbon black diverted to India and South-East Asia at low prices after EU sanctions; Indian spot prices under pressure
US tariff on Indian goods raised to 50% (PCBL effective ~20%); GST cut defers vehicle purchases; crude falls to ~$63
India-EU FTA concluded; India-US trade deal lowers tariffs
West Asia conflict: Brent $60 → ~$100-120; freight and CBFS costs up; tyre makers build inventory ('just-in-case')
Strikes on Russian refineries cut Russian CBFS and carbon black exports; Chinese suppliers raise prices

peersNote: Himadri Speciality (HSCL) is the only other listed Indian carbon black maker (plus coal-tar pitch and battery materials; net cash). Apollo Tyres and CEAT are customers (context for demand and pricing power). Aarti Industries, Deepak Nitrite and Vinati Organics are specialty-chemical names on file (benchmark for the 'specialty' multiple). Birla Carbon, Continental Carbon and Epsilon Carbon (Indian rivals) are unlisted.

street.thesis: Import mix turns favourable: Russian imports down ~40%, Chinese material dearer; guidance of ~₹17,000/t could prove conservative; FY28E EBITDA/t ₹17,500
Inventory gains aided Q1; muted FY27 guidance (₹17k/t) limits upside; awaits Aquapharm roadmap; volumes +7% CAGR FY26-28E
Profitability jumped partly on non-recurring factors; likely Q2 hiccup and inventory losses if crude falls; Aquapharm recovery gradual
Q1 above expectations; carbon black sales +20% YoY on higher realisations
Ex-inventory gains EBITDA +8% YoY to ~₹340 cr; Aquapharm below exit-quarter guidance; ramp-up lagging

moat.evidence: 900 kt, India's largest and 6th globally; five plants near ports and tyre hubs; 40% of volume exported to 45+ countries
Buys CBFS at international prices (~90% imported); no captive feedstock yet; coal-tar distillation still at feasibility stage
Formula pass-through to tyre majors; spot prices set by Russian/Chinese imports and Indian overcapacity; EBITDA/t fell from ~₹19,200 (FY25) to ~₹14,200 (FY26)
4th largest globally (company); volume 15 kt (FY15) → 70 kt (FY26), +23% YoY in Q1FY27; ~70% exported to strategic customers
122 MW co-generation from tail gas; FY26 power segment PBIT ₹239 cr (25% of segment profit) with no fuel cost
India's largest and world's 3rd largest phosphonate maker, but EBITDA fell from ₹417 cr (FY23, pre-deal) to ₹162 cr (FY26); Europe shifting to green chelates; oil & gas volatile
US process patent for nano-silicon; 80 t pilot only; no customer qualification or revenue yet

critiques.point: The Aquapharm deal has destroyed value so far: ₹3,800 cr for ₹417 cr of EBITDA (FY23) that is now ₹162 cr; Chemicals segment PBIT ₹17 cr on ₹4,226 cr of assets
Leverage is stuck: TD/PBILDT 5.0x in FY26 vs CARE's 4x trigger; all three agencies moved to Negative outlook in 2026; Andhra plant to be debt-funded
Q1FY27 was flattered by ~₹70 cr of inventory gains and a power-price spike; underlying EBITDA ~₹326-340 cr
Guidance credibility: Aquapharm ₹300 cr FY26 and ₹75 cr exit-quarter targets missed by ~46-61%; ₹20-22/kg carbon black aspiration vs ₹14.9/kg delivered
Vision 2030 (₹4,000 cr EBITDA) relies on ₹1,400 cr from battery materials that have no revenue yet
Governance: ₹35 cr (FY26) and ₹44.5 cr (FY25) of political contributions; ₹464 cr of balance-sheet investments in group companies; promoter warrants at ₹280
Bull case: Russian supply shock and US/EU trade deals give Indian producers pricing power; EBITDA/t guidance could prove conservative
